chapter: Learning the trade in Los Angeles
title: Kid Ory, Mutt Carey and New Orleans musicians in California
summary: He played jobs with Kid Ory, knew Mutt Carey, and explains why many New Orleans musicians who came with King Oliver stayed on the West Coast.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: He might have. Because in California in those days you never knew who you were going to ....... I used to play with Kid Ory on certain jobs.
Well what was Kid Ory doing there then?
He was living out there and playing.
Yes? What was that other, Mutt Carey.
Mutt Carey was out there.
Well, now did you run into him much?
Yes, quite often.
Well did he, was he any influence on you?

No except that he used to tell me little stories about the old musicians in New Orleans. And he used to call us, you know, like we were young, youngsters and then he'd tell us little things about the trumpet and little stories. But he never tried to show us anything, teach us anything.
Well he was quite a, he made a good bit of use of mute I think didn't he?
Yes.
I think so, I seem to remember that, or later on he did, I don't know whether he was doing so then.
Yes, he used the mute quite a bit. Padd Mutt, yes.
Well there were quite a lot of New Orleans musicians out there at that time weren't there?
At that, at one time there were. Yes, you see because earlier there had been a quite a bit, quite a few of them Stage out there with King Oliver. King Oliver played in Frisco for a long time.
Oh, I'd forgotten that.

Yes, he played in Frisco, and some of the guys never went back. Some of them just moved on down to Los Angeles. One of them named Montudie, [Ed Garland] bass player. They were all still out there, when I got there.
Of course, New Orleans is a fair way West any way so that it isn't quite such a .....
Yes. But I remember, you see this is before, but I do know that King Oliver went out there and he liked it very well.
Yes.
He stayed out there.
Well how long was he out there? Jelly Roll well then of course (Morton) as you said was out there.
Jelly Roll
Right. That's right. was there. Quite a few of the guys went out.
Yes, that's interesting.
I can't remember all of them. Buster, Buster Wilson. I can't remember all their names. Some, a few of them are still there, I doubt if they are still playing now.
